lessons.title: Lesson 1: Introduction to PHP Syntax
lessons.html:
Lesson 1: Introduction to PHP Syntax

PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is a popular server-side scripting language that is widely used for web development.

Basic Syntax Elements:

  • The PHP Tag: Use
  • echo: A command to output data to the screen.

Example:

<?php echo Hello, World!; ?>

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Control Structures (Conditions and Loops)
lessons.html:
Lesson 2: Control Structures

Control structures allow you to direct the flow of execution in your code.

Conditions:

Use if, else, and switch to execute code based on conditions.

if ($a > $b) { echo a is greater than b; } else { echo b is greater than a; }

Loops:

For and while loops allow executing the same block of code multiple times.

for ($i = 0; $i < 5; $i++) { echo $i; }

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Classes and Objects
lessons.html:
Object-Oriented PHP

PHP supports full OOP with classes, inheritance, interfaces, and traits.

Class Definition:

<?php
class User {
    // Properties with type declarations
    private int $id;
    public string $name;
    protected string $email;
    public readonly string $createdAt;

    // Constructor promotion (PHP 8+)
    public function __construct(
        int $id,
        string $name,
        string $email,
        private int $age = 0
    ) {
        $this->id = $id;
        $this->name = $name;
        $this->email = $email;
        $this->createdAt = date('Y-m-d H:i:s');
    }

    // Methods
    public function introduce(): string {
        return "Hi, I'm {$this->name} and I'm {$this->age} years old";
    }

    // Static method
    public static function createGuest(): self {
        return new self(0, 'Guest', 'guest@example.com');
    }

    // Getter/Setter
    public function getEmail(): string {
        return $this->email;
    }
}

$user = new User(1, 'Alice', 'alice@example.com', 30);
echo $user->introduce();

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create a BlogPost class with title, content, author, and tags
  2. Add a constructor that accepts all properties
  3. Implement a static factory method

Key Takeaways:

  • Properties can have visibility modifiers (public, private, protected)
  • Constructor promotion reduces boilerplate
  • readonly properties can only be set once

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Inheritance & Traits
lessons.html:
Inheritance and Code Reuse

PHP supports single inheritance and traits for horizontal code reuse.

Inheritance:

<?php
abstract class Vehicle {
    protected string $make;
    protected string $model;

    public function __construct(string $make, string $model) {
        $this->make = $make;
        $this->model = $model;
    }

    abstract public function getFuelType(): string;

    public function getInfo(): string {
        return "{$this->make} {$this->model}";
    }
}

class Car extends Vehicle {
    private int $doors;

    public function __construct(string $make, string $model, int $doors) {
        parent::__construct($make, $model);
        $this->doors = $doors;
    }

    public function getFuelType(): string {
        return "Gasoline";
    }
}

// Traits
interface Loggable {
    public function getLogData(): array;
}

trait Timestampable {
    private DateTime $createdAt;
    private DateTime $updatedAt;

    public function initializeTimestamps(): void {
        $this->createdAt = new DateTime();
        $this->updatedAt = new DateTime();
    }

    public function touch(): void {
        $this->updatedAt = new DateTime();
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Create an Employee/Manager inheritance hierarchy
  2. Implement a Loggable trait with activity logging
  3. Add Timestampable behavior to multiple models

Key Takeaways:

  • PHP supports single class inheritance
  • Traits enable horizontal code reuse across unrelated classes
  • Abstract classes define common interfaces with partial implementation

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Namespaces & Autoloading
lessons.html:
Organizing PHP Code

Namespaces prevent naming conflicts. PSR-4 autoloading automatically loads classes.

Namespace Structure:

<?php
// src/Models/User.php
namespace App\Models;

class User {
    public function __construct() {
        echo "User model created\n";
    }
}

// src/Services/UserService.php
namespace App\Services;

use App\Models\User;
use App\Repositories\UserRepository;

class UserService {
    private UserRepository $repo;

    public function __construct(UserRepository $repo) {
        $this->repo = $repo;
    }

    public function register(array $data): User {
        // Business logic
        return $this->repo->create($data);
    }
}

PSR-4 Autoloading:

// composer.json
{
    "autoload": {
        "psr-4": {
            "App\\": "src/"
        }
    },
    "autoload-dev": {
        "psr-4": {
            "Tests\\": "tests/"
        }
    }
}

// Then run: composer dump-autoload

// Usage
require 'vendor/autoload.php';

use App\Models\User;
use App\Services\UserService;

$user = new User();

Practice Exercises:

  1. Organize a project with namespaces following PSR-4
  2. Create a Facade class that delegates to sub-namespaces
  3. Set up autoloading for a custom library

Key Takeaways:

  • Namespaces map to directory structure
  • PSR-4 autoloading loads classes on demand
  • Use statements import classes into the current namespace

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Error Handling & Logging
lessons.html:
Robust Error Handling

PHP provides try/catch for exceptions and Monolog for structured logging.

Exception Handling:

<?php
use Monolog\Logger;
use Monolog\Handler\StreamHandler;

// Create logger
$log = new Logger('app');
$log->pushHandler(new StreamHandler('logs/app.log', Logger::WARNING));

class PaymentException extends \RuntimeException {
    public function __construct(
        string $message,
        private int $paymentId,
        int $code = 0,
        ?Throwable $previous = null
    ) {
        parent::__construct($message, $code, $previous);
    }

    public function getPaymentId(): int {
        return $this->paymentId;
    }
}

function processPayment(int $paymentId, float $amount): void {
    try {
        if ($amount <= 0) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException("Amount must be positive");
        }

        if ($amount > 10000) {
            throw new PaymentException("Amount exceeds limit", $paymentId);
        }

        // Process payment...
        echo "Payment processed\n";

    } catch (InvalidArgumentException $e) {
        $log->error('Validation failed: ' . $e->getMessage());
        throw $e;  // Re-throw
    } catch (PaymentException $e) {
        $log->error('Payment failed', [
            'payment_id' => $e->getPaymentId(),
            'error' => $e->getMessage()
        ]);
        // Handle accordingly
    } finally {
        echo "Payment attempt finished\n";
    }
}

Practice Exercises:

  1. Set up Monolog with multiple handlers (file + email)
  2. Create custom exception hierarchy for a domain
  3. Implement global exception handler with HTTP response

Key Takeaways:

  • Try/catch handles recoverable errors
  • Custom exceptions carry domain-specific context
  • Structured logging with Monolog is production-ready

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Dependency Injection
lessons.html:
DI Containers and Service Providers

Dependency Injection creates loosely coupled, testable code. Containers manage service resolution.

Manual DI:

<?php
interface LoggerInterface {
    public function log(string $message): void;
}

class FileLogger implements LoggerInterface {
    public function log(string $message): void {
        file_put_contents('logs/app.log', $message . PHP_EOL, FILE_APPEND);
    }
}

class UserController {
    public function __construct(
        private UserRepository $repo,
        private LoggerInterface $logger
    ) {}

    public function show(int $id): array {
        $this->logger->log("Fetching user $id");
        return $this->repo->find($id);
    }
}

// Wiring
$logger = new FileLogger();
$repo = new UserRepository(new DatabaseConnection('localhost', 'db', 'user', 'pass'));
$controller = new UserController($repo, $logger);

PHP-DI Container:

use DI\ContainerBuilder;

$builder = new ContainerBuilder();
$builder->addDefinitions([
    // Auto-wiring: LoggerInterface maps to FileLogger
    LoggerInterface::class => DI\autowire(FileLogger::class),

    // Parameter binding
    DatabaseConnection::class => DI\autowire()
        ->constructorParameter('host', 'localhost')
        ->constructorParameter('dbname', 'myapp'),

    // Factory
    UserService::class => DI\factory(function (Container $c) {
        return new UserService(
            $c->get(UserRepository::class),
            $c->get(CacheService::class)
        );
    }),
]);

$container = $builder->build();
$controller = $container->get(UserController::class);

Practice Exercises:

  1. Refactor a class to use constructor DI
  2. Create a service provider for a third-party library
  3. Implement auto-wiring with PHP Reflection

Key Takeaways:

  • DI reduces coupling between classes
  • Containers manage the object graph
  • Auto-wiring resolves dependencies automatically
